project.name: vjepa_visual_localization
project.goal: Build a camera-only visual localization system using V-JEPA latent representations. During mapping, ground-truth pose is available and stored with visual embeddings. During online localization, GPS/ground-truth pose is unavailable; the system estimates current pose by retrieving and matching V-JEPA embeddings against the prebuilt visual map.
project.long_term_goal: Use the same architecture as a foundation for autonomous-driving visual localization without OCR or manually assigned semantic landmark IDs.
core_constraints: Do not require semantic labels for signs, shelves, buildings, road signs, or landmarks.
Warehouse aisles can look highly repetitive.
Small visual details such as location signs may be the most discriminative visual landmarks.
People, forklifts, boxes, vehicles, and other dynamic objects may appear during mapping or localization.
The first implementation must prioritize a working baseline before advanced research features.
Use V-JEPA visual/video representations as the primary learned representation.
Ground-truth pose is available only during mapping and evaluation.

research_hypothesis.main: Global V-JEPA embeddings can provide coarse place retrieval, while local V-JEPA patch/tubelet tokens can preserve discriminative local landmarks that distinguish visually repetitive warehouse aisles.
research_hypothesis.dynamic_object_hypothesis: Persistent static visual landmarks will produce repeated correspondences across traversals, while people and other dynamic objects will be inconsistent and can be down-weighted without explicit segmentation.
research_hypothesis.target_pipeline: global retrieval -> local token matching -> geometric verification -> temporal consistency -> motion prior -> pose estimation

implementation_principles: Save intermediate embeddings and retrieval scores for analysis.
Avoid hard-coding four frames per two seconds; expose clip duration and number of sampled frames as configuration parameters.
Use coarse-to-fine retrieval so local token matching is only performed on a small candidate set.
Keep mapping and online-localization code paths separate.
Do not add OCR as a fallback.

pose_definition.yaw: camera or robot heading in radians

data_format.synchronization: Each sampled video clip must be assigned the ground-truth pose corresponding to the clip center timestamp.

video.resize: use the preprocessing required by the selected V-JEPA checkpoint

dds_image_transport.network: direct Ethernet LAN; both hosts use the same ROS_DOMAIN_ID

dds_orin_results.pose_semantics: GPS-like x/y/yaw in the warehouse map frame; not latitude/longitude
dds_orin_results.latent_type: std_msgs/msg/Float32MultiArray with the current normalized 1024-D query embedding
dds_orin_results.debug_type: std_msgs/msg/String JSON containing clip timestamp, compute host, inference latency, selected source, top-k candidates/scores, similarity and temporal state
dds_orin_results.evaluation_boundary: Gazebo truth remains on the laptop dashboard and is never an Orin localization input

VisualMap.local_token_storage: separate or lazy-loaded storage indexed by map entry id

stage_0_dataset_pipeline.goal: Create synchronized video clips and poses.
tasks: For every clip center timestamp, sample a fixed-duration video clip.
Uniformly sample num_sampled_frames from the clip.
Interpolate or select the nearest ground-truth pose at the clip center time.
Return clip tensor, pose, timestamp, and unique id.
Write unit tests for timestamp synchronization.
acceptance_criteria: Dataset iteration returns deterministic clip/pose pairs.
Clip timestamps and pose timestamps differ by less than a configurable tolerance.
Visual inspection utility can save sample clips with associated pose metadata.

stage_1_vjepa_encoder.goal: Wrap V-JEPA behind a clean interface.

global_embedding.baseline: mean-pool local output tokens over token dimension

local_tokens.postprocess: L2 normalize each token along feature dimension
local_tokens.note: Keep spatial/temporal token ordering metadata if the V-JEPA implementation exposes it.

tests: Embeddings contain no NaN or Inf.
L2 normalized global vectors have norm approximately one.
Identical clips produce nearly identical embeddings in eval mode.

stage_2_global_mapping.goal: Build the first visual map using only global embeddings.
algorithm: Store timestamp and map entry id.
stage_2_global_mapping.note: Do not introduce FAISS until brute-force cosine retrieval is verified.

stage_3_global_baseline_localization.goal: Establish the simplest working localization baseline.
query_algorithm: Compute cosine similarity against all map global embeddings.
Use top-1 candidate pose as the initial prediction.

optional_weighted_pose.formula: w_i = exp(alpha * score_i); pose = sum(w_i * pose_i) / sum(w_i)
optional_weighted_pose.warning: Only interpolate nearby candidates. Do not average poses from spatially disconnected map locations.

stage_4_metrics.yaw_error: smallest wrapped angular difference between yaw_gt and yaw_pred
stage_4_metrics.important: Evaluate query runs from different traversals than mapping runs whenever possible.

stage_5_local_token_map.goal: Add local V-JEPA token storage for fine matching.
stage_5_local_token_map.reason: Global embeddings may be dominated by generic warehouse geometry and fail to preserve small distinctive signs or local landmarks.
storage_strategy: Store local tokens separately by map entry id.
Load local tokens only for globally retrieved top-K candidates.
Optionally compress or select tokens later if storage becomes excessive.

stage_6_local_token_matching.goal: Re-rank global retrieval candidates using local token correspondences.
stage_6_local_token_matching.similarity_matrix: S = Q @ M.T after L2 normalization
basic_matching: For each query token q_i, find max cosine similarity over candidate tokens.
Collect best score and best candidate-token index.
Do not average all query tokens.
Select top K strongest token correspondences.
Average only the selected top-K scores.
notes: Weights are hyperparameters, not fixed research claims.
The hypothesis is that small distinctive location signs become high-confidence local matches without OCR.

stage_7_spatial_and_geometric_verificati.goal: Reject visually similar but geometrically inconsistent candidates.
stage_7_spatial_and_geometric_verificati.prerequisite: Preserve the spatial position of local V-JEPA tokens or map tokens back to image/video coordinates.
pipeline: Keep high-confidence mutual or near-mutual matches.
Convert token ids to approximate image coordinates.
Estimate a geometric model using RANSAC.
Possible models: homography for approximately planar/local scenes, fundamental matrix for general two-view geometry.
Score candidate using number of geometric inliers and reprojection/epipolar error.
Re-rank candidate list using appearance score plus geometric score.
stage_7_spatial_and_geometric_verificati.important: Do not require semantic knowledge of what a matched patch represents.

stage_8_temporal_sequence_localization.goal: Use multiple consecutive query clips so a temporary occlusion or dynamic object cannot dominate localization.
stage_8_temporal_sequence_localization.concept: Match a sequence of query embeddings against a spatially/temporally consistent sequence in the stored map.
better_version: Search a local temporal/spatial window around candidate map indices.
Use dynamic programming or beam search for the highest-scoring consistent map trajectory.
Penalize impossible jumps between map locations.

example.behavior: If q2 is occluded by a pedestrian, q0, q1, and q3 can still preserve the correct sequence hypothesis.

stage_9_motion_prior.goal: Resolve perceptual aliasing using robot motion.
inputs: wheel odometry and/or IMU if available

first_version.logic: Reject candidates that require physically impossible displacement from the previous estimated pose.

stage_9_motion_prior.example: If previous pose is near (11,4), a visually similar candidate at (45,18) should be rejected unless the motion model permits such displacement.

stage_10_dynamic_object_robustness.goal: Reduce influence of people, forklifts, vehicles, and temporarily moved objects without OCR and preferably without explicit segmentation.
stage_10_dynamic_object_robustness.phase_1: Rely on local matching plus temporal consistency; dynamic patches should have fewer stable correspondences.

method: Associate map observations from approximately the same spatial region across traversals.
Estimate how often each local visual pattern reappears.
Assign each pattern a persistence score.

expected_behavior.forklift: low or medium persistence depending on parking behavior

stage_11_pose_estimation.mvp: Return pose of best map entry.
improved: Use only spatially nearby top candidates.
Weight poses by final candidate scores.
Handle yaw using circular averaging rather than linear averaging.
advanced: If local correspondences and camera calibration permit, estimate relative camera pose.
Combine relative pose with known mapped landmark/camera poses.
Fuse visual measurement with motion filter.

required_experiments: Global retrieval + local V-JEPA token matching.
Persistent-landmark weighting with multiple mapping traversals.
environment_splits: objects moved between mapping and query
experimental_matrix.research_question: How much does each component improve robustness under perceptual aliasing and dynamic-scene changes?

development_order.name: V-JEPA wrapper
development_order.deliverable: Global embedding and optional local tokens.

development_order.name: Map extraction
development_order.deliverable: Saved global map embeddings and poses.

development_order.name: Global cosine baseline
development_order.deliverable: Top-k retrieval and top-1 pose prediction.

codex_instructions.role: Act as the implementation engineer for this repository.
workflow: Read this entire specification before modifying code.
Inspect the existing repository before creating files.
Implement stages in development_order unless the repository already contains equivalent functionality.
Do not silently change the core architecture.
Add tests for each core module.
Do not add OCR or text recognition.
Do not assume signs contain readable text; treat them only as visual patterns.
Do not hard-code warehouse-specific semantic IDs.
When unsure about V-JEPA output tensor structure, inspect the installed/official model implementation and adapt the wrapper while preserving the public encode_video API.
After each implementation stage, run relevant tests and provide a concise summary of changed files and known limitations.

first_task.objective: Implement only Stage 0 through Stage 4 first.
first_task.stop_condition: Stop after the global baseline is functional and evaluated. Do not implement local token matching until baseline metrics and retrieval outputs can be inspected.

engineering: End-to-end command can build a visual map from a mapping run.
End-to-end command can localize clips from a separate query run.
research: Can compare global-only localization to local-token-based localization.
Can evaluate robustness when pedestrians and moving objects are present.
Can quantify perceptual aliasing failures in repetitive warehouse aisles.
Architecture can later be tested on road-driving video without changing its dependence on semantic labels.
